trust_decision.summary: Evaluated code must never end the embedding process: any BaseException-only class the symbol table hands to the sandbox (SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt, BaseException) that sandbox code raises has to become an asteval ExceptionHolder error at the interpreter boundary and must not be re-raised by the conversion path, while ordinary exceptions keep their class and procedure state is still restored.

landing_point.why: The summary says a BaseException subclass escapes; an engineer greps `except Exception` and lands on run()'s handler guard, the one place where an exception raised by a node handler is turned into an asteval error, so the first fix attempt is to widen this clause.

fix_sites.entry_point: Interpreter.eval (the raise_errors re-raise of the recorded class)
sandbox function call from Interpreter.eval (on_call boundary to host callables and Procedures)
every path that reports an error through Interpreter.raise_exception, including Interpreter.eval
Procedure.__call__ (astutils.py:643), invoked by on_call at asteval.py:955 and directly by a host holding the Procedure
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level call machinery in the astutils module (state save/restore + re-raise)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Procedure.__call__ reads as internal bookkeeping that deliberately re-raises the body's exception to a direct caller (tests/test_asteval.py:1769-1794), so a solver argues it must not swallow anything and leaves its `except Exception as exc` untouched, even though a BaseException there skips the symtable/code_text/_calldepth restore at astutils.py:751-755.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A procedure body's own exception must still reach a host that calls the Procedure directly with its original class (ZeroDivisionError stays ZeroDivisionError) and the interpreter must stay reusable afterwards, which is what tests/test_asteval.py:1769-1794 asserts; a fix that turns every exception crossing Procedure.__call__ into a swallowed asteval error, instead of only reclassifying the exiting BaseException-only classes, breaks that contract.

O6_input_shapes: `raise SystemExit(1)` / `raise SystemExit()`: the class comes from the symtable (astutils.py:99) and on_raise raises the instantiated class through raise_exception (asteval.py:916-920), so the escaping class is `out.__class__`
`raise KeyboardInterrupt()`: same path, class exported at astutils.py:94
`raise BaseException('x')`: the bare BaseException class is exported at astutils.py:90 and is not an Exception subclass

`raise SystemExit` with no call does NOT escape: on_raise reads `out.args` on the class object (asteval.py:916), the resulting AttributeError is converted, so a solver who tests only the bare name sees nothing wrong

the same raise inside a sandbox-defined function body, which additionally skips Procedure.__call__'s state restore (astutils.py:747-755) and corrupts the interpreter even when the host catches the exception

a BaseException-only exception propagated from a host-supplied callable or object (user_symbols function, property read in safe_getattr at astutils.py:309-312, operator dunder) invoked by sandbox code at asteval.py:954-961

O7_producer.where: asteval/astutils.py:89-110 (FROM_PY list) and asteval/astutils.py:522-566 (BUILTINS_TABLE / make_symbol_table installing the names, e.g. symtable.update(BUILTINS_TABLE) at astutils.py:552)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Interpreter.run(node, with_raise=True) called directly by a host: run's widened except catches the exiting class at asteval.py:322, but its conversion call re-raises the recorded SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt from inside the except block (asteval.py:324 -> 258-264), so the exception still leaves run()
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: run() is the low-level sibling of the documented eval(); a solver treats 'the eval path is fixed' as sufficient and the direct-run caller as responsible for catching its own exceptions (run is called directly at tests/test_asteval.py:1308).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 0 files: same function as the landing point, leaking through raise_exception in the same file (asteval/asteval.py:249-264)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Interpreter.eval(..., raise_errors=True) re-raises the recorded error class at asteval.py:376-379, so an evaluated `raise SystemExit(1)` still reaches the caller as SystemExit after the except clauses are widened
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: raise_errors=True is the documented opt-in that re-raises errors (tests/test_asteval.py:1611-1622 asserts a NameError reaches the caller), so a solver reads 'the caller asked for exceptions' as out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 0 files: same function as the landing point (asteval/asteval.py:347-380)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second symbol-table route (the nested Group table, or a restricted/user_symbols merge) that also installs SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt/BaseException because it copies FROM_PY
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: make_symbol_table is the only place symbols are installed and already has two layouts (plain dict at astutils.py:550-554 and nested Group at 559-564); a maintainer adding a restricted or hosted table would copy the same builtins block.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A comprehension save/restore block (on_listcomp/on_dictcomp) that restores shadowed symbols only on the normal path, exactly like Procedure.__call__
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both functions deep-copy shadowed names (asteval.py:857, 871) and restore them after iteration (861-862, 875-876); a BaseException during iteration skips the restore, so a maintainer who fixed the Procedure case would plausibly have left this one as written.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A safe_* wrapper (safe_getattr / SafeFormatter.get_field) that must also convert BaseException-only errors coming from a host object's property or __format__
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: These wrappers already funnel host-object failures into raise_exception (safe_getattr's raise_exc argument, SafeFormatter at astutils.py:320-328); a maintainer extending the containment to callbacks would naturally add the check beside them.

O9_family: sandbox containment failure: an exiting BaseException subclass raised by evaluated code propagates out of the interpreter (CWE-248 uncaught exception; CWE-184 incomplete denylist of exception names installed in the symbol table)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools>=45 + setuptools_scm>=6.2 (pyproject.toml:1-7), pytest with --cov=asteval (pyproject.toml:15-16); asteval/version.py is generated by setuptools_scm (pyproject.toml:6) and imported by asteval/__init__.py:1, so the raw tree must be built/installed before import; numpy is optional (astutils.py:28-34)
O10_build.project_tests: single pytest module tests/test_asteval.py (about 1800 lines; all but test_py3 are parametrized over nested_symtable False/True); exception-area tests: test_raise 942-946, test_tryexcept 948-979, test_tryelsefinally 981-1006, test_recursionlimit 1259-1263, test_kaboom 1265-1288, test_raise_errors_unknown_symbol 1610-1623, test_partial_exception 1522-1535, test_lambda_exception_cleared 1768-1794; there is no test naming SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt or BaseException anywhere in the tree

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Widen the six `except Exception` clauses in asteval/asteval.py to `except BaseException`; it still leaks because the conversion re-raises the recorded exiting class (asteval.py:324 -> 249-264, and eval:376-379) and a BaseException leaving a procedure body still skips the state restore at astutils.py:747-755.

out_of_scope_notes: asteval/asteval.py:781-783: on_with calls ctx.__exit__() with no arguments, which would TypeError for any ordinary context manager; a prototype bug unrelated to this advisory, not pursued.

asteval/asteval.py:890-895: on_try's handler matching calls e_type() on self.error[-1].exc_info, which is (None, None, None) for errors raised through raise_exception outside a Python except block, so a sandbox `except SomeError:` around a sandbox `raise` can itself fail; separate from this advisory.
unverified: The provided fix diff (scr-2068.fix.diff) contains only the 5-line merge-commit header for a3e56e7 with no diff hunks, so fix_sites and j_sites_touched are inferred from the advisory summary plus the classifier metadata (c_same_check_sites=6, c_site_files=2, c_restructured=1) and from reading the pinned code; which hunks the published fix actually changed could not be checked.

O1 counts Interpreter.eval/__call__, Interpreter.run and Procedure.__call__ as the distinct public entries that reach the flaw; Procedure is not in asteval/__init__.py:__all__ but is the value sandbox functions live in and is callable by a host.

O2 (Procedure.__call__ in astutils.py) is placed as a fix site on the inference that the second changed source file is astutils.py; if the published fix only touched the six asteval.py except clauses, that site is an uncovered route rather than part of the fix.

Whether the published fix reclassifies the recorded exception in raise_exception (asteval.py:249-264) or instead strips SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt/BaseException from FROM_PY (astutils.py:89-110) could not be checked; the two routes differ in whether a host-delivered KeyboardInterrupt is still propagated.
